formalFindings: PER Art1.1: Electrical Engineering bachelor with Automotive Technology core; post2023 entrants. Art3.3 English; Appendix2.2f full-time. Public major page confirms BSc Electrical Engineering specialized in Automotive, no standalone degree.

Art3.4:180EC, core125 including calculus/CBL5/BEP10, ITEC10 and electives45. Appendix2 pp73–74 confirms all27 current positions; curriculumPDF separately verifies codes/credits. No optional autonomy/perception/electric-drive courses added to core.

Art3.4.8/3.7 and elective page:30EC level2/3 including15EC level3, no core/elective or intra-elective overlap, prerequisites/timeslots, programme approval via PlanApp. Genuine elective space kept open15+30.

Appendix2.2e p78 and project page:120EC including all mandatory first-year units; nominal first two years120 meet it. Project ordinaryQ3/Q4 year3, alternativeQ1 with advisor permission.10EC plus optional5 from electives, not extra compulsory credit.
CBL challenge entry: previous offered embedded P&PD communication/collaboration/planning units completed; nominal preceding components meet it. P&PD/challenges embedded, not extra credits.
Art3.4.5–6 and corresponding pages:five SG ITEC-logo activities;MyFuture activity valueatleast7; both non-credit. Normal firstyear BSA45/60, nominal60meets.

Current PDF title4AUB10 Propulsion Systems vs PER older electric/hybrid powertrain label: samecode5ECrequired, not separate courses. New title retained; detailed specific-engine teaching not presumed. No essential identity/status/credit conflict.

Public bachelor description establishes connected/self-driving/software/electronics and smarter/cleaner/safer system interests; explicitly not specifically trained to develop a car. No MSc Smart/Sustainable tracks imported.
